themes_detail.label: Construction surge and plumbing emergencies
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints spiked to 64 THIS WEEK versus a 12.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 397% increase (z-score: 10.52)—suggesting either a major construction project or systemic plumbing failures affecting multiple buildings in Midwood.
evidence: 64 construction/plumbing complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.9-complaint weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 10.52 indicates statistically extreme deviation
322 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days, with 242 alterations—context for ongoing construction activity
reporting_angles: Identify which construction project(s) are driving the spike—canvas affected blocks for resident complaints about noise, dust, water shutoffs
Interview NYC Department of Buildings on whether there are open violations or emergency permits related to plumbing infrastructure in the district

themes_detail.label: Street noise and obstruction explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 59 THIS WEEK from a 14.5-complaint weekly average (307% spike, z-score: 5.47), while sidewalk obstructions nearly tripled to 11 THIS WEEK versus 4.4 average (151% spike, z-score: 5.44)—indicating a concentrated disruption to pedestrian and residential conditions.
evidence: 59 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 14.5-complaint weekly baseline (307% increase)
11 obstruction complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.4-complaint weekly baseline (151% increase)
Both spikes occurred in the same week, suggesting a single event or concentrated construction/event activity
reporting_angles: Locate ongoing street work, event permits, or street fairs issued this week in Midwood—cross-reference with 311 complaint addresses
Interview residents on Avenues J, K, or main commercial corridors (Coney Island Ave, Nostrand Ave) to identify the source and duration of noise

themes_detail.label: Waste management and cleanup crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 27 TWO WEEKS AGO from a 5.8-complaint weekly average (370% increase, z-score: 7.11), while dumpster complaints and abandoned bikes both surged 2300% two weeks ago (3 complaints each vs. 0.1 average, z-score: 8.69)—pointing to a waste collection failure or illegal dumping event.
evidence: 27 residential disposal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 5.8-complaint weekly baseline (370% spike)
3 dumpster complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1-complaint weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
3 abandoned bikes 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1-complaint weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)—suggests streets left unclean
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to determine if there was a service disruption, strike, or equipment failure two weeks ago in CD 314
Visit blocks with high concentrations of disposal and dumpster complaints to assess current sanitary conditions and interview residents about collection patterns

themes_detail.label: Pest infestation uptick—pigeons
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary pigeon complaints surged 700% to 4 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 0.5-complaint weekly average (z-score: 4.95), suggesting clustering of pigeon-related nuisance reports in a specific area—possibly tied to waste accumulation or food sources.
evidence: 4 unsanitary pigeon complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5-complaint weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
Spike aligns temporally with residential disposal and dumpster spikes, suggesting common cause (waste management failure)
reporting_angles: Map the four pigeon complaints geographically—are they clustered around a specific business, park, or residential block?
Interview NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene on pigeon mitigation efforts and whether this spike prompted any response

themes_detail.label: Underground infrastructure stress—roots and sewers
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints more than doubled to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO from a 1.4-complaint weekly average (191% spike, z-score: 5.42), indicating potential subsurface damage or aging infrastructure failure affecting sidewalk and drainage systems.
evidence: 4 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.4-complaint weekly baseline (191% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Long-standing theme: heat/hot water complaints remain the district's #1 issue at 5,578 over 90 days—many may be plumbing-related
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with DEP for recent main breaks, service calls, or inspections in Midwood two weeks ago
Visit addresses with root/sewer complaints to photograph sidewalk damage and interview residents on water pressure, backing up, or flooding issues
